evals.prompt: I run a small church, ELICM, and our 16th anniversary celebration is Oct 18 with a free dinner and guest speaker. Registration page is https://elicm-anniversary.example.com. We want Facebook ads to get people in our city (mostly families and older adults within 15 miles) to register. Budget is about $15/day for 3 weeks. Give me everything I need to run the ads.
evals.expected_output: A complete copy-paste ad pack: 3+ angles of single-image ads with primary text/headline/description/CTA and creative briefs, a carousel, at least one short video script with shot list, campaign structure with budget, launch checklist, and a review from the expert panel. Should be respectful of religion-related targeting/policy limits.
expectations: Contains at least 3 distinct single-image ads each with primary text, headline, description/CTA button
Contains a carousel with every card's image concept and headline written out
Contains at least 2 video scripts laid out with timing, visual, and spoken line (filmable shot table)
Each ad has a creative brief specifying format/aspect ratio (e.g. 4:5, 9:16) and on-image text
Includes campaign structure: objective, audience/location settings, budget, and schedule
Includes a success metric plus explicit kill/scale rules (when to pause, when to raise budget)
Ads use at least 3 structurally different hook families (e.g. callout, story, proof, contrarian, question) rather than rewordings
Includes a landing page message-match or ad-scent check
No copy uses second-person diagnosis of a personal attribute (health, religion, age, financial status) in a way Meta would reject
Includes a review/critique pass showing what was changed (expert panel or equivalent)
No placeholder text like [insert], TBD, or lorem ipsum in ad copy fields
Copy states the event is free and names Oct 18 in headline or first 125 chars of at least one ad
Campaign plan phases the 3 weeks (announce / remind / last call) rather than flat spend
Targeting recommendation uses geography rather than religion as a targeting attribute
